'''''The Master''''' is a 2012 American [[Historical drama|period]] [[psychological drama]] film written and directed by [[Paul Thomas Anderson]] and starring [[Joaquin Phoenix]], [[Philip Seymour Hoffman]], and [[Amy Adams]]. It tells the story of Freddie Quell (Phoenix), a [[World War II]] [[United States Navy|Navy]] veteran struggling to adjust to a post-war society, who meets Lancaster Dodd (Hoffman), the leader of a cult known as The Cause. Dodd sees something in Quell and accepts him into the movement. Quell takes a liking to The Cause and begins traveling with Dodd's family to spread his teachings.

The film was produced by [[Annapurna Pictures]] and Ghoulardi Film Company and distributed by [[The Weinstein Company]]. The film's inspirations were varied: it was partly inspired by [[Scientology]] founder [[L. Ron Hubbard]], early drafts of Anderson's ''[[There Will Be Blood]]'', the novel ''[[V.]]'' by [[Thomas Pynchon]], [[John Huston]]'s documentary ''[[Let_There_Be_Light_(1946_film)|Let There Be Light]]'' about WWII veterans with [[PTSD]], drunken Navy stories that [[Jason Robards]] had told to Anderson while filming ''[[Magnolia (film)|Magnolia]]'', and the life story of author [[John Steinbeck]]. ''The Master'' was shot almost entirely on 65 mm film stock, making it the first fiction feature to be shot and released in [[70 mm film|70mm]] since [[Kenneth Branagh]]'s ''[[Hamlet (1996 film)|Hamlet]]'' in 1996.

Initially, the film was set up with [[Universal Pictures]], but fell through due to script and budget problems. It was first publicly shown on August 3, 2012, at the [[American Cinematheque]] in 70&nbsp;mm and screened variously in the same way, before officially premiering at the [[69th Venice International Film Festival|Venice Film Festival]] on September 1, where it won three awards: the [[International Federation of Film Critics|FIPRESCI Award]] for Best Film; the [[Silver Lion]] for Anderson's direction; and the [[Volpi Cup for Best Actor]], shared by Phoenix and Hoffman. It was released in theaters in the United States on September 14, 2012, to critical acclaim; its performances (particularly those from the three leads), screenplay, direction, plausibility, and realistic portrayal of post-World War II Americans were praised.

Considered one of Anderson's finest works and one of the [[List of films voted the best|best films]] of the 2010s and the 21st century, it received three [[Academy Awards|Oscar]] nominations: [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] for Phoenix, [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] for Hoffman, and [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]] for Adams. In 2016, ''The Master'' was ranked the 24th in the [[BBC's 100 Greatest Films of the 21st Century]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.com/culture/story/20160819-the-21st-centurys-100-greatest-films|title=The 21st Century's 100 greatest films|date=August 19, 2016|access-date=December 17, 2021|archive-date=January 31, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170131124228/http://www.bbc.com/culture/story/20160819-the-21st-centurys-100-greatest-films|url-status=live}}</ref> Anderson has repeatedly stated that ''The Master'' is his favorite film of those he has made.<ref>{{cite web|title='The Master' Is Paul Thomas Anderson's Favorite Movie, Even If He's 'Not Sure It Was Entirely Successful'|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2018/02/paul-thomas-anderson-the-master-favorite-film-1201931234/|website=IndieWire|date=February 22, 2018 |access-date=March 14, 2018|archive-date=March 14, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314174553/http://www.indiewire.com/2018/02/paul-thomas-anderson-the-master-favorite-film-1201931234/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Plot==
<!-- Per [[MOS:FILMPLOT]], plot summaries for feature films should be between 400 to 700 words. -->
In early 1950, Freddie Quell is a [[hypersexuality|sex-obsessed]] [[alcoholism|alcoholic]] [[United States Navy|Navy]] [[veteran]] struggling to adjust to post-war society in the wake of [[World War II]]. Prone to violent and erratic behavior, he is fired from his job as a department store photographer after getting into a fight with a customer. He works on a [[Filipino Americans|Filipino-American]] community farm in California until an elderly colleague collapses after drinking Freddie's [[moonshine]]. Freddie is accused of poisoning him and flees.

In [[San Francisco, California|San Francisco]], Freddie stows away on the yacht of a follower of Lancaster Dodd, the charismatic leader of a philosophical movement known as "The Cause." When he is discovered, Dodd describes Freddie as "aberrated" and claims to have met him in the past but cannot remember where. He invites Freddie to stay to attend the marriage of his daughter, and to make more moonshine for which Dodd has developed a taste. Dodd begins an exercise with Freddie called "processing," in which he asks Freddie a flurry of disturbing psychological questions. Freddie breaks down at the end of the exercise while recalling his past relationship with Doris, a girl from his hometown to whom he promised to return.

Freddie travels with Dodd's family as they spread The Cause along the East Coast. Dodd's family consist of his wife, Peggy, his adult children, Val and Elizabeth, and Elizabeth's new husband, Clark. While at a dinner party in New York, a man accuses The Cause of being a [[cult]]. Dodd berates him and asks him to leave. Freddie pursues the man and assaults him, to Dodd's dismay. Dodd's wife Peggy starts having misgivings about Freddie's presence.

Freddie criticizes Dodd's son, Val, for disregarding his father's teachings, but Val says Dodd is making it up as he goes along. Dodd is arrested for practicing medicine without qualifications; Freddie attacks the police officers and is also taken into custody. In jail, Freddie erupts in an angry tirade, questioning everything Dodd taught him, and accusing him of being a fake. Dodd calls Freddie lazy and worthless, claiming nobody but Dodd likes him. Upon release, they reconcile, but members of The Cause have become suspicious and fearful of Freddie, believing him to be deranged, an undercover agent, or simply beyond help. Dodd insists Freddie's behavior can be corrected with rigorous conditioning, which Freddie struggles to internalize.

Freddie accompanies Dodd to [[Phoenix, Arizona]], to celebrate the release of Dodd's book. When Dodd's publisher criticizes it, Freddie assaults him. Dodd loses his temper with acolyte Helen Sullivan after she questions inconsistencies between the new book and Dodd's previous publications. Dodd takes a group to a [[Salt pan (geology)|salt flat]] for a game consisting of picking a point in the distance and riding towards it on Dodd's motorcycle. Freddie takes his turn but does not return, disappearing into the horizon.

Freddie returns home to [[Lynn, Massachusetts]], to visit Doris, but learns from her mother that she has married and started a family. Sleeping in a movie theater, Freddie receives a phone call from Dodd begging him to visit him in England, where he now resides. Deciding to go, Freddie finds The Cause has grown ever larger. The previously skeptical Val is now a high-ranking member of The Cause, while Elizabeth and Clark have been expelled from the organization. Peggy rebuffs Freddie as being a lost cause, but Dodd is still hopeful that he can sway Freddie back to the fold. Dodd recounts that, in a past life, they had worked together in Paris sending balloons across a Prussian blockade. Dodd gives Freddie an ultimatum: devote himself to the Cause for life, or leave and never return. As Freddie suggests that they may meet again in the next life, Dodd says that if they do, it will be as sworn enemies. Dodd sings "[[On a Slow Boat to China]]" as Freddie weeps. Freddie leaves and picks up a woman at a pub, repeating questions from his first processing session as he is having sex with her. 

On a beach, Freddie curls up to a crude sand sculpture of a woman he and his Navy comrades sculpted during the war.

==Production==

===Writing===

It was first reported in December 2009 that [[Paul Thomas Anderson]] had been working on a script about the founder of a new religious organization (described as being similar to [[Scientology]]) played by [[Philip Seymour Hoffman]].<ref name="Vancouver">{{cite web |last=Konjicanin |first=Anja |url=http://www.vancouverobserver.com/blogs/artsbeat/2011/05/10/paul-thomas-anderson%E2%80%99s-scientology-film-back-track |title=Paul Thomas Anderson's Scientology film back on track |publisher=Can Do Media Inc. |work=[[The Vancouver Observer]] |date=May 10, 2011 |access-date=June 2, 2011 |archive-date=October 6, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006073327/http://www.vancouverobserver.com/blogs/artsbeat/2011/05/10/paul-thomas-anderson%E2%80%99s-scientology-film-back-track |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Variety">{{cite web |last=Fleming |first=Michael |title=Anderson working on 'Master' |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |publisher=[[Reed Business Information]] |date=December 2, 2009 |url=https://variety.com/2009/film/markets-festivals/anderson-working-on-master-1118012101/ |access-date=June 5, 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121108043403/http://www.variety.com/article/VR1118012101?refCatId=13 |archive-date=November 8, 2012 }}</ref> An associate of Anderson stated that the idea for the film had been in Anderson's head for about twelve years.<ref name="NYTimes">{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Cieply |title=Filmmaker's Newest Work Is About ... Something |work=[[The New York Times|NYTimes.com]] |date=April 18, 2012 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/22/movies/paul-thomas-anderson-film-may-be-about-scientology.html?_r=2&pagewanted=all |access-date=April 18, 2012 |archive-date=December 20, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220114458/http://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/22/movies/paul-thomas-anderson-film-may-be-about-scientology.html?_r=2&pagewanted=all |url-status=live }}</ref> The idea for the film came to him after reading a quote stating that periods after wars are productive times for spiritual movements to start.<ref name=dailybeast/>

Unsure of the direction the script would take, Anderson began writing ''The Master'' as a collection of disparate scenes, rather than one coherent outline.<ref name=dailybeast>{{cite journal | url = http://www.thedailybeast.com/newsweek/2012/08/19/inside-the-master-paul-thomas-anderson-s-supposed-scientology-movie.html | title = Inside 'The Master', Paul Thomas Anderson's Supposed "Scientology" Movie | date = August 20, 2012 | access-date = August 21, 2012 | first = David | last = Ansen | journal = [[The Daily Beast]] | publisher = [[The Newsweek Daily Beast Company]] | archive-date = January 18, 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130118082554/http://www.thedailybeast.com/newsweek/2012/08/19/inside-the-master-paul-thomas-anderson-s-supposed-scientology-movie.html | url-status = live }}</ref> He combined unused scenes from early drafts of ''[[There Will Be Blood]]'', elements from the life stories of [[John Steinbeck]] and [[L. Ron Hubbard]] and from the novel ''[[V.]]'' by [[Thomas Pynchon]], and stories [[Jason Robards]] had told him on the set of ''[[Magnolia (film)|Magnolia]]'' about his drinking days in the U.S. Navy during [[World War II]] (including the draining of [[torpedo juice|ethanol from a torpedo]]).<ref name=dailybeast/> Anderson conducted research about [[Dianetics]] and its early followers.<ref name="npr">{{cite web |last=Campbell |first=Christopher |title=Paul Thomas Anderson, The Man Behind 'The Master' |work=NPR.com |publisher=[[NPR]] |date=October 3, 2012 |url=https://www.npr.org/2012/10/02/162153952/paul-thomas-anderson-the-man-behind-the-master# |access-date=October 2, 2012 |archive-date=October 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121003074329/http://www.npr.org/2012/10/02/162153952/paul-thomas-anderson-the-man-behind-the-master |url-status=live }}</ref> While writing, Anderson sought Hoffman's feedback on the script, with Hoffman suggesting the film focus more on Freddie's story than Lancaster's.<ref name=dailybeast/> After the film was dropped by Universal and failed to pick up a distributor, Anderson did several months of rewrites.<ref name="VillageVoice"/>

===Casting===

Anderson has stated that he wanted Hoffman to play Lancaster Dodd from the film's inception, and that he also had [[Joaquin Phoenix]] in mind for the part of Freddie Quell.<ref name=dailybeast/> [[Jeremy Renner]] and [[James Franco]] were each rumored to play Freddie before Phoenix was officially attached.<ref name="Greenlight"/><ref name="Renner">{{cite web |last=Campbell |first=Christopher |title=Jeremy Renner Joins Paul Thomas Anderson's Religious Cult Movie |work=MTV.com |publisher=[[MTV Networks]] |date=March 17, 2010 |url=http://moviesblog.mtv.com/2010/03/17/jeremy-renner-may-join-paul-thomas-anderson-the-maste |access-date=June 5, 2011 |archive-date=January 11, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111052623/http://moviesblog.mtv.com/2010/03/17/jeremy-renner-may-join-paul-thomas-anderson-the-maste/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|last=Valby|first=Karen|title=James Franco 'wasn't scared enough' to have a role in 'The Master'|url=http://insidemovies.ew.com/2012/10/19/james-franco-the-master/|magazine=Entertainment Weekly|access-date=October 20, 2012|archive-date=October 22, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022232316/http://insidemovies.ew.com/2012/10/19/james-franco-the-master/|url-status=live}}</ref> This was Phoenix's first screen appearance since the 2010 film ''[[I'm Still Here (2010 film)|I'm Still Here]]'', a multi-year [[performance art]] [[mockumentary]] project that Phoenix attributed as a factor in limiting the roles he was subsequently offered.<ref name="Sperling"/><ref name="lim">{{cite news |author=Lim, Dennis |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/09/05/movies/joaquin-phoenix-bounces-back-in-the-master.html?_r=0&adxnnl=1&adxnnlx=1349222556-YN/8QtgDqUoCxC/yRQPcBA |title=A Star Swerves a Bit; He's Fine With That |work=The New York Times |date=September 4, 2012 |access-date=October 2, 2012 |archive-date=March 12, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180312204724/http://www.nytimes.com/2012/09/05/movies/joaquin-phoenix-bounces-back-in-the-master.html?_r=0&adxnnl=1&adxnnlx=1349222556-YN%2F8QtgDqUoCxC%2FyRQPcBA |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Reese Witherspoon]] was reportedly offered the role of Peggy Dodd, but [[Amy Adams]] was later cast.<ref name="AmyAdams">{{cite web |last=Jagernauth |first=Kevin |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/archives/amy_adams_joins_paul_thomas_andersons_the_master |title=Amy Adams Joins Paul Thomas Anderson's 'The Master' |publisher=indieWire |work=The Playlist |date=June 1, 2011 |access-date=June 3, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604045617/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/archives/amy_adams_joins_paul_thomas_andersons_the_master |archive-date=June 4, 2011 }}</ref><ref name="Witherspoon">{{cite web |last=Davis |first=Edward |url=https://theplaylist.blogspot.com/2010/05/reese-witherspoon-offered-role-in-paul.html |title=Reese Witherspoon Offered A Role In Paul Thomas Anderson's Untitled Religion Pic? Shooting Starting In June? |publisher=indieWire |work=The Playlist |date=May 24, 2010 |access-date=June 5, 2011 |archive-date=August 18, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818130909/http://theplaylist.blogspot.com/2010/05/reese-witherspoon-offered-role-in-paul.html |url-status=live }}</ref> For the role of Dodd's daughter, [[Amanda Seyfried]], [[Emma Stone]], and [[Deborah Ann Woll]] were all considered, with the role eventually going to [[Ambyr Childers]].<ref name="Childers">{{cite web |last=Dang |first=Simon |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/general/little-known-ambyr-childers-books-ptas-the-master-ruben-fleischers-gangster-squad-115992/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125113401/https://www.indiewire.com/news/general/little-known-ambyr-childers-books-ptas-the-master-ruben-fleischers-gangster-squad-115992/ |url-status=live |archive-date=January 25, 2025 |title=Little-Known Ambyr Childers Books PTA's 'The Master' & Ruben Fleischer's 'Gangster Squad' |publisher=indieWire |work=The Playlist |date=October 4, 2011 |access-date=October 9, 2011 }}</ref>

|access-date=November 6, 2012 |archive-date=October 18, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018014313/http://www.in70mm.com/news/2012/the_master/photography/index.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Originally, Anderson and Mălaimare planned to shoot mainly portraits in 65 mm, which constituted 20 percent of the film, but ultimately 85 percent of the film was shot in 65 mm.<ref name="65mmkodak">{{cite web |url=http://motion.kodak.com/motion/Publications/InCamera/The_Master_Framed_in_65mm_for_Maximum_Visual_Impact.htm|title=The Master: Framed in 65 mm for Maximum Visual Impact |publisher=www.kodak.com|work=[[Eastman Kodak]] |date=September 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121012005026/http://motion.kodak.com/motion/Publications/InCamera/The_Master_Framed_in_65mm_for_Maximum_Visual_Impact.htm |access-date=September 30, 2012|archive-date=October 12, 2012 }}</ref> The remainder of the film was shot on [[35mm movie film|35mm]] using [[Panavision cameras#Panaflex Millennium|Panavision Millennium XL2s]] cameras, often used for scenes that required a "dirtier" look.<ref name="65mmkodak"/> In order to maintain a consistent [[Aspect ratio (image)|aspect ratio]], the 65 mm footage was cropped from 2.20:1 to 1.85:1 to match the 35 mm footage, at the sacrifice of some image area.<ref name="65mmkodak"/> Most of the [[film stock]]s used were [[Vision 3|Kodak Vision3 50D Color Negative Film 5203]] and Kodak Vision3 200T Color Negative Film 5213 with a few scenes also done with Kodak Vision3 250D Color Negative Film 5207 and Kodak Vision3 500T 5219.<ref name="65mmkodak"/> Because Anderson prefers working with film, he bypassed the use of a [[digital intermediate]], instead [[color grading]] with the use of a photochemical timer.<ref name="editPC"/>

During filming, Phoenix was allowed to improvise on set.<ref name="Sperling"/> Phoenix lost significant weight for the role and came up with Freddie's awkward gait.<ref name="Sperling">{{cite web |author=Sperling, Nicole |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/moviesnow/la-et-mn-joaquin-phoenix-20120909,0,5184139,full.story |title=Joaquin Phoenix takes unpredictable path in 'The Master' |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=September 8, 2012 |access-date=October 2, 2012 |archive-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120920220731/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/moviesnow/la-et-mn-joaquin-phoenix-20120909,0,5184139,full.story |url-status=dead }}</ref> Anderson compared Phoenix's commitment to that of [[Daniel Day-Lewis]] for his level of concentration, saying that Phoenix got into character and stayed there for three months.<ref name=dailybeast/><ref name="lim"/> Anderson considered the dynamic between Hoffman and Phoenix to be central to the film, likening it to the rivalry and differences in style and temperament between tennis players [[John McEnroe]] and [[Björn Borg]] or [[Ivan Lendl]], with Hoffman playing the more controlled and driven approach of Borg or Lendl.<ref>{{cite news|author=Brooks, Xan|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2014/feb/03/philip-seymour-hoffman-great-modern-american-cinema|title=Philip Seymour Hoffman was the one great guarantee of modern American cinema|newspaper=The Guardian|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=February 17, 2014|archive-date=February 22, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222193955/http://www.theguardian.com/film/2014/feb/03/philip-seymour-hoffman-great-modern-american-cinema|url-status=live}}</ref> Adams stated that Anderson would have her appear on set for scenes she was not scheduled to appear in to make her presence felt, and at times she didn't know whether the camera was on her.<ref name="adamsinterview">{{cite web |last=Shone |first=Tom |url=https://www.vulture.com/2012/08/amy-adams-the-master.html |title=Amy Adams's Spiritual Revival |work=Vulture |publisher=[[New York (magazine)|New York Magazine]] |date=August 19, 2012 |access-date=August 22, 2012 |archive-date=August 21, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120821200318/http://www.vulture.com/2012/08/amy-adams-the-master.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Music===
{{Main|The Master (soundtrack)}}
[[Jonny Greenwood]] of [[Radiohead]] composed the [[Film score|score]] for the film.<ref name="Greenwood" /><ref name="Pitchfork">{{cite web|last=Battan|first=Carrie|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/44848-jonny-greenwood-confirmed-to-score-new-paul-thomas-anderson-film/|title=Jonny Greenwood Confirmed to Score New Paul Thomas Anderson Film|website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |date=December 8, 2011 |access-date=November 20, 2014|archive-date=September 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140906074341/http://pitchfork.com/news/44848-jonny-greenwood-confirmed-to-score-new-paul-thomas-anderson-film/|url-status=live}}</ref> This was the second time Greenwood scored an Anderson film, the first being 2007's ''[[There Will Be Blood]]''.<ref name="Greenwood">{{cite web |last=Jagernauth |first=Kevin |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/there-will-be-jonny-greenwood-radiohead-member-to-score-paul-thomas-andersons-the-master |title=Jonny Greenwood To Score Paul Thomas Anderson's 'The Master' |publisher=indieWire |work=The Playlist |date=December 5, 2011 |access-date=December 5, 2011 |archive-date=June 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130627025257/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/there-will-be-jonny-greenwood-radiohead-member-to-score-paul-thomas-andersons-the-master |url-status=live }}</ref>

The official soundtrack was released through [[Nonesuch Records]], and comprises eleven compositions by Greenwood along with four recordings from the film's era. Performers include the [[London Contemporary Orchestra]] and [[Ella Fitzgerald]], among others.<ref name="Nonesuch">{{cite web |url=http://www.nonesuch.com/albums/the-master-soundtrack |title='The Master' Soundtrack |work=Nonesuch.com |date=September 17, 2012 |access-date=September 24, 2012 |archive-date=September 23, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120923083315/http://www.nonesuch.com/albums/the-master-soundtrack |url-status=live }}</ref> The track "[[Don't Sit Under the Apple Tree (with Anyone Else but Me)]]" is presented as performed in the film by actress [[Madisen Beaty]]. The Weinstein Company also released a more comprehensive score on their website as part of the film's promotion, featuring alternate versions of the tracks.<ref name="The Weinstein Company">{{cite web |url=http://twcguilds.com/film/the-master#score |title='The Master' Score |work=twcguilds.com |date=December 31, 2012 |access-date=September 30, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130302033447/http://twcguilds.com/film/the-master#score |archive-date=March 2, 2013}}</ref>

==Release==

===Distribution===

''The Master'' was initially set up with [[Universal Pictures|Universal]], but, like [[The Weinstein Company]], they eventually passed on the project because of problems with the script.<ref name="Vancouver" /><ref name="Variety" /> Universal was mainly concerned with the excessive budget of about $35 million.<ref name="NYTimes" /> It was later reported that River Road was in serious talks to fully finance the film.<ref name="RiverRoad">{{cite web |last=Fleming |first=Mike |url=https://deadline.com/2010/03/pta-taking-river-road-on-religion-pic-with-phil-hoffman-and-jeremy-renner-28617/ |title=Paul Thomas Anderson Talking Religion With Philip Seymour Hoffman And Jeremy Renner |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |publisher=[[Mail.com Media|Mail.com Media Corporation]] |date=March 16, 2011 |access-date=June 5, 2011 |archive-date=June 7, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607035832/http://www.deadline.com/2010/03/pta-taking-river-road-on-religion-pic-with-phil-hoffman-and-jeremy-renner/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2011, it was reported that [[Megan Ellison]], daughter of billionaire [[Larry Ellison]], would finance ''The Master'' and Anderson's adaptation of the novel ''[[Inherent Vice]]'' under her new production company [[Annapurna Pictures]].<ref name="NYTimes" /><ref name="NYMag2">{{cite web |last=Brodesser-Akner |first=Claude |title=Paul Thomas Anderson's Scientology Movie and Inherent Vice Adaptation Close to Finding Financing |publisher=New York Media Holdings |work=[[New York (magazine)|NYMag.com]] |date=February 10, 2011 |url=https://nymag.com/daily/entertainment/2011/02/paul_thomas_anderson.html |access-date=June 5, 2011 |archive-date=May 22, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110522021216/http://nymag.com/daily/entertainment/2011/02/paul_thomas_anderson.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Harvey Weinstein]] later picked up the worldwide rights to the film in May 2011.<ref name="Greenlight" /><ref name="Vancouver" /><ref name="NYTimes" />

===70 mm screenings===

The film was the first in 16 years to be predominantly shot in 65 mm (using Panavision System 65 cameras), a camera negative format that is subsequently projected in 70 mm (the extra 5 mm are added to the projection prints to accommodate the audio tracks). On August 3, 2012, more than a month before its first official screening at the Venice Film Festival, ''The Master'' was shown in a "surprise screening" at the [[American Cinematheque]] in [[70 mm film|70&nbsp;mm]].<ref name=elsewhere/><ref name=hitflix/><ref name=chitribune>{{cite news |last=Phillips |first=Michael |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2012/08/17/once-is-not-enough-for-the-master/ |title=Once is not enough for 'The Master' |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=August 17, 2012 |access-date=September 12, 2012 |archive-date=September 11, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911133015/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2012-08-17/entertainment/ct-mov-0817-talking-pictures-20120817_1_film-foundation-festival-program-notes-music-box |url-status=live }}</ref> It was announced that there would be a special screening just after a screening of a new remastered version of [[Stanley Kubrick]]'s ''[[The Shining (film)|The Shining]]''.<ref name=elsewhere/><ref name=hitflix/> Following the credits of ''The Shining'', it was announced that the special screening was ''The Master''.<ref name=elsewhere/><ref name=hitflix/> The film was shown with no opening titles (except for the title of the movie) or closing credits.<ref name=elsewhere>{{cite news |first=Jeff |last=Wells |url=http://hollywood-elsewhere.com/2012/08/the_master_snea.php |title=The Master Sneaks at Aero |work=Hollywood-Elsewhere.com |date=August 4, 2012 |access-date=August 4, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120807054615/http://hollywood-elsewhere.com/2012/08/the_master_snea.php |archive-date=August 7, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=hitflix>{{cite news |first=Kristopher |last=Tapley |url=http://www.hitfix.com/in-contention/first-public-screening-of-paul-thomas-andersons-the-master-happening-right-now-in-santa-monica |title=First public screening of Paul Thomas Anderson's 'The Master' happening right now in Santa Monica |work=[[HitFix]] |date=August 4, 2012 |access-date=August 4, 2012 |archive-date=August 5, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120805181430/http://www.hitfix.com/in-contention/first-public-screening-of-paul-thomas-andersons-the-master-happening-right-now-in-santa-monica |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Weinstein Company continued [[Film screening|advance screenings]] of the film in 70&nbsp;mm in [[New York City]], [[Los Angeles]], [[London]], [[Chicago]], [[San Francisco]], [[Seattle]], [[Boston]], [[Washington, D.C.]], and [[Austin, Texas|Austin]].<ref name=chitribune/> Although this was done because there was strong consideration that ''The Master'' was unlikely to be shown in the format during its commercial run, the film was eventually displayed during its run in 70&nbsp;mm in most cinemas that carried the film and could still project that format.<ref name="VillageVoice"/>

===Home media===
The film was released on [[DVD]] and [[Blu-ray]] on February 26, 2013, in the US, and March 11 in the UK. The release features "Back Beyond", a twenty-minute montage of deleted footage edited by Paul Thomas Anderson and set to Jonny Greenwood's original score. It also includes the 1946 [[John Huston]] documentary ''[[Let There Be Light (1946 film)|Let There Be Light]]'', a source which Anderson reportedly found very influential in his creation of the film.<ref name="Blu-Ray.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=10263 |title='The Master BluRay Release Details |work=twcguilds.com |date=January 14, 2013 |access-date=January 19, 2013 |archive-date=January 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130122015259/http://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=10263 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="The Playlist at Indiewire.com">{{cite web |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/i-dont-consider-that-were-dealing-with-a-cult-paul-thomas-anderson-talks-about-the-master-at-tiff-20120909 |title='"I Don't Consider That We're Dealing With A Cult" - Paul Thomas Anderson Talks About 'The Master' At TIFF |work=indiewire.com |date=September 9, 2012 |access-date=January 19, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121030083326/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/i-dont-consider-that-were-dealing-with-a-cult-paul-thomas-anderson-talks-about-the-master-at-tiff-20120909 |archive-date=October 30, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Reception==

===Box office===

''The Master'' grossed $242,127 at five theaters during its opening day on September 14, 2012, setting a single-day record for an [[Art film|art house film]].<ref name="BoxOffice">{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/box-office-scientology-master-resident-evil-370578 |first=Pamela |last=McClintock |title=Box Office Report: Scientology-Inspired 'The Master' Shatters Art House Records |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]] |date=September 15, 2012 |access-date=September 17, 2012 |archive-date=September 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120916204016/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/box-office-scientology-master-resident-evil-370578 |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall the film made $736,311 from five theaters for a per-theater average of $147,262, setting a record for the highest average for a live-action film. During its first week nationwide, the film grossed $4.4 million in 788 theaters.<ref name="BoxOfficeMojoWide">{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=3530&p=.htm |first=Ray |last=Subers |title=Weekend Report: 'End of Watch' Narrowly Beats 'House', 'Curve' |work=[[Box Office Mojo]] |publisher=[[Internet Movie Database]] |date=September 23, 2012 |access-date=September 30, 2012 |archive-date=September 25, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120925233831/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=3530&p=.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Critical response===
{{multiple images
| total_width = 325
| direction = horizontal
| align = right
| image1 = Joaquin Phoenix at the 2018 Berlin Film Festival.jpg
| image2 = Philip Seymour Hoffman 2011.jpg
| footer = Both [[Joaquin Phoenix|Phoenix]] and [[Philip Seymour Hoffman|Hoffman]]’s performances were lauded by critics, and won them the [[Volpi Cup for Best Actor]]. They were both nominated for [[Academy Awards]] for their performances, which were considered to be among their finest.
| alt1 = 
}}
On [[review aggregator]] [[Rotten Tomatoes]], ''The Master'' has an approval rating of 85% based on 257 reviews. The website's critical consensus reads, "Smart and solidly engrossing, ''The Master'' extends Paul Thomas Anderson's winning streak of challenging films for serious audiences."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_master_2011 |title=The Master (2012) |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media]] |access-date=August 14, 2021 |archive-date=March 28, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328011854/http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_master_2011/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film has a [[weighted average]] score of 86 out of 100, based on 43 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-master |title=The Master Reviews |work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=CBS Interactive |access-date=September 24, 2012 |archive-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120920065032/http://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-master |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Kenneth Turan]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', in praising Anderson's directing and Phoenix's performance, wrote: "Phoenix, known for immersing himself in Oscar-nominated roles in ''[[Gladiator (2000 film)|Gladiator]]'' and ''[[Walk the Line]]'', makes Quell frighteningly believable." About the film itself, he stated: "''The Master'' takes some getting used to. This is a superbly crafted film that's at times intentionally opaque, as if its creator didn't want us to see all the way into its heart of darkness."<ref name="Turan">{{cite web |author=Turan, Kenneth |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/moviesnow/la-et-mn-the-master-20120914,0,4243764.story |title=Review: 'The Master' mesmerizes in word and deed |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=September 13, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=September 19, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120919163538/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/moviesnow/la-et-mn-the-master-20120914,0,4243764.story |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Lisa Schwarzbaum]] of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' gave the film a perfect "A" grade, stating: "It's also one of the great movies of the year - an ambitious, challenging, and creatively hot-blooded, but cool-toned, project that picks seriously at knotty ideas about American personality, success, rootlessness, master-disciple dynamics, and father-son mutually assured destruction."<ref name="Schwarzbaum">{{cite magazine |author=Schwarzbaum, Lisa |url=https://ew.com/article/2012/10/19/master-2/ |title='The Master' Review |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |date=September 19, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=October 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016030723/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20620111,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Amy Adams at NYFF 2013.jpg|thumb|145px|[[Amy Adams|Adams]] was also praised by critics and received her fourth [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nomination for her performance.]]
Peter Rainer of ''[[The Christian Science Monitor]]'' wrote that "the performances by Phoenix and Hoffman are studies in contrast. Phoenix carries himself with a jagged, lurching, simian-like grace, while Hoffman gives Dodd a calm deliberateness. Both actors have rarely been better in the movies. The real Master class here is about acting – and that includes just about everybody else in the film, especially Adams, whose twinkly girl-next-door quality is used here to fine subversive effect."<ref name="Rainer">{{cite web |author=Rainer, Peter |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/The-Culture/Movies/2012/0914/Movie-review-Writer-director-Paul-Thomas-Anderson-s-The-Master-draws-us-in-video |title=Movie review: Writer-director Paul Thomas Anderson's 'The Master' draws us in |work=CSMonitor.com |date=September 14, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=September 19, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120919185033/http://www.csmonitor.com/The-Culture/Movies/2012/0914/Movie-review-Writer-director-Paul-Thomas-Anderson-s-The-Master-draws-us-in-video |url-status=live }}</ref> [[A. O. Scott]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' wrote: "It is a movie about the lure and folly of greatness that comes as close as anything I've seen recently to being a great movie. There will be skeptics, but the cult is already forming. Count me in."<ref name="Scott">{{cite web |author=Scott, A. O. |url=https://movies.nytimes.com/2012/09/14/movies/review-the-master-from-paul-thomas-anderson.html?ref=movies&_r=0 |title=There Will Be Megalomania |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=September 13, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=November 9, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121109061642/http://movies.nytimes.com/2012/09/14/movies/review-the-master-from-paul-thomas-anderson.html?ref=movies&_r=0 |url-status=live }}</ref> Scott Tobias of ''[[The A.V. Club]]'', giving the film an "A" grade, wrote: "It's a feisty, contentious, deliberately misshapen film, designed to challenge and frustrate audiences looking for a clean resolution. Just because it's over doesn't mean it's settled."<ref name="Tobias">{{cite web |author=Tobias, Scott |url=https://www.avclub.com/the-master-1798174159 |title=The Master |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |publisher=Onion Inc |date=September 13, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120920075125/http://www.avclub.com/articles/the-master,84866/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Peter Travers]] of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' gave the film four stars out of four, praising Anderson's directing: "''The Master'', the sixth film from the 42-year-old writer-director, affirms his position as the foremost filmmaking talent of his generation. Anderson is a rock star, the artist who knows no limits." About the film itself, he wrote: "Written, directed, acted, shot, edited, and scored with a bracing vibrancy that restores your faith in film as an art form, ''The Master'' is nirvana for movie lovers. Anderson mixes sounds and images into a dark, dazzling music that is all his own." He would later call the film the Best Film of 2012.<ref name="Travers">{{cite web |author=Travers, Peter |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/reviews/the-master-20120910 |title=The Master |work=RollingStone.com |date=September 10, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012}}</ref>

[[Todd McCarthy]] of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' wrote: "In a film overflowing with qualities, but also brimming with puzzlements, two things stand out: the extraordinary command of cinematic technique, which alone is nearly enough to keep a connoisseur on the edge of his seat the entire time, and the tremendous portrayals by Joaquin Phoenix and Philip Seymour Hoffman of two entirely antithetical men, one an unlettered drifter without a clue, the other an intellectual charlatan who claims to have all the answers. They become greatly important to each other and yet, in the end, have an oddly negligible mutual effect. The magisterial style, eerie mood and forbidding central characters echo Anderson's previous film, ''There Will Be Blood'', a kinship furthered by another bold and discordant score by [[Jonny Greenwood]]."<ref name="McCarthy">{{cite web |author=McCarthy, Todd |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/master-philip-seymour-hoffman-joaquin-phoenix-367129 |title='The Master': Venice Review |work=The Hollywood Reporter |date=September 1, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=September 18, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120918125837/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/master-philip-seymour-hoffman-joaquin-phoenix-367129 |url-status=live }}</ref> Justin Chang of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' magazine wrote: "The writer-director's typically eccentric sixth feature is a sustained immersion in a series of hypnotic moods and longueurs, an imposing picture that thrillingly and sometimes maddeningly refuses to conform to expectations."<ref name="Chang">{{cite web |author=Chang, Justin |url=https://www.variety.com/review/VE1117948152 |title=The Master |work=Variety |publisher=Reed Elsevier Properties Inc |date=September 1, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=October 4, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004024401/http://www.variety.com/review/VE1117948152/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[James Berardinelli]] of ''[[ReelViews]]'' gave the film three stars out of four and praised Phoenix's performance, stating: "Gaunt, sick-looking, with stooped shoulders and a shambling gait, Phoenix buries himself in Freddie's persona and there's never a moment when we disbelieve him." He added: "Yet, for all of ''The Master''{{'}}s laudable elements, it falls short of greatness for one simple reason: the storytelling is unspectacular."<ref name="Berardinelli">{{cite web |author=Berardinelli, James |url=http://www.reelviews.net/php_review_template.php?identifier=2518 |title=Master, The |work=ReelViews.net |date=September 14, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=October 23, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023060316/http://www.reelviews.net/php_review_template.php?identifier=2518 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Even less enthusiastic was [[Roger Ebert]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'', who gave the film two-and-a-half stars out of a possible four. He wrote that it was "fabulously well-acted and crafted, but when I reach for it, my hand closes on air. It has rich material and isn't clear what it thinks about it. It has two performances of Oscar caliber, but do they connect?"<ref name="Ebert">{{cite web |author=Ebert, Roger |date=September 19, 2012 |title=The Master |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-master-2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130602064258/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-master-2012 |archive-date=June 2, 2013 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |work=Chicago Sun-Times |publisher=RogerEbert.com}}</ref> However, Ebert later included ''The Master'' as an honorable mention on his list of the best films of 2012, naming it alongside nine other titles he granted his Grand Jury Prize that year.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Ebert, Roger |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/roger-ebert/eberts-top-movies-of-2012 |title=Ebert's Top Movies of 2012 |work=RogerEbert.com |date=December 27, 2012 |access-date=June 4, 2020 |archive-date=June 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200604182444/https://www.rogerebert.com/roger-ebert/eberts-top-movies-of-2012 |url-status=live }}</ref> Calum Marsh of ''[[Slant Magazine]]'' gave the film two stars out of four, stating: "''The Master'' is Paul Thomas Anderson with the edges sanded off, the best bits shorn down to nubs."<ref name="Marsh">{{cite web |author=Marsh, Calum |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/the-master/6501 |title=The Master |work=SlantMagazine.com |date=September 10, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=September 14, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120914061431/http://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/the-master/6501 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Rex Reed]] of the ''[[New York Observer]]'' gave the film a negative review, writing: "Call ''The Master'' whatever you want, but lobotomized catatonia from what I call the New Hacks can never take the place of well-made narrative films about real people that tell profound stories for a broader and more sophisticated audience. Fads come and go, but, as Walter Kerr used to say, 'I'll yell tripe whenever tripe is served.'" Reed also made mention of how Phoenix's performance and the supporting characters' lack of development further hurt the film.<ref name="Reed">{{cite web |author=Reed, Rex |url=http://observer.com/2012/09/the-master-rex-reed-philip-seymour-hoffman-joaquin-phoenix-paul-thomas-anderson |title='The Master' Loses Control of Its Flock: Underserved Cast Overacts in Paul Thomas Anderson's Pretentious Sermon |work=Observer.com |date=September 18, 2012 |access-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-date=September 21, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120921233207/http://observer.com/2012/09/the-master-rex-reed-philip-seymour-hoffman-joaquin-phoenix-paul-thomas-anderson/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On Phoenix's performance, [[Kent Jones (critic)|Kent Jones]] of ''[[Film Comment]]'' noted, "Freddie is not so much played as nuzzled, and jerked into being by Joaquin Phoenix. ''I'm Still Here'' aside, Phoenix's Freddie seems like genuinely damaged goods. He and his director feel their way into this man-in-a-bind from the inside out, and they establish his estrangement from others in those opening scenes through awkward smiles and out-of-sync body language alone".<ref name="Jones">{{cite journal |last=Jones |first=Kent |title=Battlefield Mankind |journal=Film Comment |date=September–October 2012 |volume=48 |issue=5 |pages=24–28 |url=http://www.filmcomment.com/article/the-master-paul-thomas-anderson-review |access-date=September 24, 2012 |archive-date=September 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120920063036/http://www.filmcomment.com/article/the-master-paul-thomas-anderson-review |url-status=live }}</ref> "As always with Anderson," Jones continued, "the character opposition borders on the schematic, and the structure threatens to come apart at the seams. But the courting of danger is exactly what makes his films so exciting, this new film most of all. I don't think he has ever done a better job of resolving his story, perhaps because he has come to terms with the irresolution within and between his characters."<ref name="Jones" /> Scott, of ''The New York Times'', pointed out that Phoenix used "sly, manic ferocity" to portray Freddie as "an alcoholic wreck".<ref name="Scott" />

Emma Dibdin of ''[[Total Film]]'' gave ''The Master'' 5 stars out of 5, concluding that it "is a breath-taking, singular, technically audacious film, white-hot with emotion, and boasting a few scenes so individually powerful that they'll stay with you like a physical presence for days".<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Dibdin|first=Emma|title=The Master review|url=http://www.totalfilm.com/reviews/cinema/the-master-1|magazine=[[Total Film]]|access-date=November 6, 2012|date=October 26, 2012|archive-date=October 28, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121028215521/http://www.totalfilm.com/reviews/cinema/the-master-1|url-status=live}}</ref>

''The Master'' was placed #1 in both the critics poll of the best films of 2012 by ''[[Sight and Sound]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/race/master-tops-sight-sound-critics-396608|title='The Master' Tops 'Sight & Sound' Critics Poll|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=December 1, 2012|access-date=April 17, 2020|archive-date=February 25, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225160310/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/race/master-tops-sight-sound-critics-396608|url-status=live}}</ref> and by ''[[The Village Voice]]'' on its [[Village Voice Film Poll|annual film poll]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.villagevoice.com/2012-12-19/film/the-2012-voice-film-critics-poll/|title=The 2012 Voice Film Critics' Poll|author=Foundas, Scott|newspaper=[[The Village Voice]]|date=December 19, 2012|access-date=December 19, 2012|archive-date=December 22, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121222045246/http://www.villagevoice.com/2012-12-19/film/the-2012-voice-film-critics-poll/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The film also ranked second by both {{italic correction|''[[Film Comment]]''}}<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.filmcomment.com/entry/50-best-films-of-2012|title=50 BEST FILMS OF 2012|magazine=[[Film Comment]]|access-date=December 19, 2012|archive-date=December 19, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121219005304/http://www.filmcomment.com/entry/50-best-films-of-2012|url-status=live}}</ref> and ''[[Indiewire]]''<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.indiewire.com/survey/indiewire-2012-year-end-critics-poll/|title=Indiewire 2012 Year-End Critics Poll|work=[[Indiewire]]|access-date=April 17, 2020|archive-date=May 31, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531022016/http://www.indiewire.com/survey/indiewire-2012-year-end-critics-poll/|url-status=live}}</ref> on their year-end film critics polls, following ''[[Holy Motors]]''.

''The Master'' was later placed #1 on ''[[The A.V. Club]]''{{'}}s list of the best films of the 2010s up until April 2015,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.avclub.com/article/100-best-films-decade-so-far-1-20-217530|title=The 100 best films of the decade (so far), #1-20|newspaper=[[The A.V. Club]]|access-date=April 17, 2020|archive-date=August 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810051830/http://www.avclub.com/article/100-best-films-decade-so-far-1-20-217530|url-status=live}}</ref> and was named as one of the top 50 films of the decade so far by ''[[The Guardian]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url = https://www.theguardian.com/film/2015/jan/05/top-50-films-of-the-demi-decade-peter-bradshaw|title = Peter Bradshaw's top 50 films of the demi-decade|last = Bradshaw|first = Peter|work = [[The Guardian]]|date = January 5, 2015|access-date = April 29, 2015|archive-date = May 29, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150529225814/http://www.theguardian.com/film/2015/jan/05/top-50-films-of-the-demi-decade-peter-bradshaw|url-status = live}}</ref>

Anderson considers it his favorite of the films he has made; in an interview with the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', he said:

<blockquote>For sure. I think that won't change. The amount of emotion I put into it and they put into it—they being Phil [Seymour Hoffman], Joaquin [Phoenix], and Amy [Adams]. I'm not sure it's entirely successful. But that's fine with me. It feels right. It feels unique to me. I really hope it will be something people can revisit and enjoy in a way that equals my pride in it. And pride can be a dangerous thing, and I'm not being very quiet about my pride in saying all this. But I just feel really proud of it. And of course, there's a particular sentimentality attached to it for a number of personal reasons. It's all wrapped up.<ref>{{cite news|url = https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/la-en-mn-paul-thomas-anderson-phantom-thread-oscars-20180220-htmlstory.html|title = 'Phantom Thread's' Paul Thomas Anderson on the Valley, daydreaming and the movie he's writing with his 8-year-old|last = Whipp|first = Glenn|work = [[Los Angeles Times]]|date = January 20, 2018|access-date = March 14, 2018|archive-date = March 13, 2018|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180313170217/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/la-en-mn-paul-thomas-anderson-phantom-thread-oscars-20180220-htmlstory.html|url-status = live}}</ref></blockquote>

In May 2025, ''[[ScreenCrush]]'' ranked the film at number 20 on its list of "The 20 Best Movies of the Last 20 Years," with Matt Singer writing "On a recent rewatch, I felt like ''The Master'' is as much a twisted love story as Anderson’s ''[[Phantom Thread]]'', and was mostly struck with the poignance of its story about a man who claims he can erase trauma suffered in past lives, who cannot even help his most fervent follower deal with the trauma he has experienced in ''this'' life."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://screencrush.com/best-movies-last-20-years/ | title=The 20 Best Movies of the Last 20 Years | date=May 1, 2025 }}</ref> In June 2025, the film ranked number 42 on ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century" and number 87 on the "Readers' Choice" edition of the list.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/best-movies-21st-century.html | title=The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century | date=June 23, 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref> In July 2025, it ranked number 44 on ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-lists/best-movies-of-the-21st-century-1235200512/ | title=100 Best Movies of the 21st Century | date=July 1, 2025 }}</ref>

==Accolades==
{{Main|List of accolades received by The Master (2012 film){{!}}List of accolades received by ''The Master'' (2012 film)}}
The film won the [[Silver Lion]] for Best Director (Paul Thomas Anderson) and the [[Volpi Cup]] for Best Actor (given to both Joaquin Phoenix and Philip Seymour Hoffman) at the [[69th Venice International Film Festival]]. However, the festival's jury originally intended to give the film the top [[Golden Lion]] prize for Best Film; the prize was removed and awarded to ''[[Pietà (film)|Pietà]]'' instead, owing to a new rule that prohibited the award of acting and directing honors to the same film that won the Golden Lion prize. A similar incident was rumored to have occurred at the festival in 2008, when [[Darren Aronofsky]]'s ''[[The Wrestler (2008 film)|The Wrestler]]'' was to be awarded both the Golden Lion and the Volpi Cup for [[Mickey Rourke]]'s performance. The film received the former, with the latter being awarded to [[Silvio Orlando]] for his work in ''[[Giovanna's Father]]''. When asked about the last-minute shake-up over the award, Anderson replied: "I'm thrilled with whatever they want to hand over. I heard some of the scuttlebutt recently, but I'm just thrilled with what they hand over. And that's all."<ref name="Huffington Post">{{cite web |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/09/08/the-master-venice-film-festival-award_n_1867317.html |title='The Master' Venice Film Festival Controversy: P.T. Anderson Film Loses Award On Technicality |first=Christopher |last=Rosen |work=[[The Huffington Post]] |publisher=[[AOL]] |date=September 8, 2012 |access-date=October 1, 2012 |archive-date=September 11, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911033123/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/09/08/the-master-venice-film-festival-award_n_1867317.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="THR">{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/venice-controversy-jury-yanks-top-the-master-368892 |title=Venice Film Festival Jury Yanks Top Prize from 'The Master' (Exclusive) |first=Matthew |last=Belloni |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]] |date=September 8, 2012 |access-date=September 9, 2012 |archive-date=September 8, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120908233216/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/venice-controversy-jury-yanks-top-the-master-368892 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="LA">{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/goldstandard/la-et-mn-venice-film-awards-20120908,0,36455.story|title='The Master' wins big at Venice ... and it could have been bigger|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=September 8, 2012|access-date=September 9, 2012|last=Whipp|first=Glenn|archive-date=September 9, far).<ref>{{Cite web |title=101 Greatest Screenplays of the 21st Century (*so far) |url=https://www.wga.org/writers-room/101-best-lists/101-best-screenplays-of-the-21st-century-so-far/list ==Themes and interpretations==

There have been several interpretations of what ''The Master'' is really about.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2012/09/what-is-the-master-really-about-five-readings.html|title=What Is The Master Really About?: Five Interpretations|date=September 25, 2012|access-date=April 17, 2020|archive-date=May 19, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200519075055/https://www.vulture.com/2012/09/what-is-the-master-really-about-five-readings.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://filmschoolrejects.com/what-is-the-meaning-of-the-master-beb730e617c3#.fzquibfaz|title=What is the Meaning of 'The Master'?|first=Christopher|last=Campbell|date=September 23, 2012|access-date=June 7, 2016|archive-date=February 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170210114428/https://filmschoolrejects.com/what-is-the-meaning-of-the-master-beb730e617c3#.fzquibfaz|url-status=live}}</ref> Some have viewed it as an existential tale of [[History of the United States (1945–1964)|post-war America]], while others have viewed it as a depiction of the birth of [[Scientology]].<ref name="Filming" /><ref name="NYMag3" /><ref name="Scientology">{{cite web |last=Yamato |first=Jen |url=http://www.film.com/movies/will-scientologists-declare-war-on-paul-thomas-andersons-the-master#fbid=Sh0pkd5XnLJ |title=Will Scientologists Declare War on Paul Thomas Anderson's The Master? |publisher=[[RealNetworks]] |work=Film.com |date=June 10, 2010 |access-date=June 2, 2011 |archive-date=June 9, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120609133843/http://www.film.com/movies/will-scientologists-declare-war-on-paul-thomas-andersons-the-master#fbid=Sh0pkd5XnLJ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Others have argued that the film is partly about acting; Richard Brody of the ''New Yorker'' observed that, "Similarly, it's perhaps notable that Phoenix's performance seems to represent the tormented, physical acting styles of the latter half of the twentieth century (the [[Marlon Brando|Brandos]], the [[James Dean|Deans]], the [[Montgomery Clift|Clifts]]), whereas Hoffman's acting seems to hearken back to the controlled, elusive manner of the previous half (many have described his turn as "[[Orson Welles|Wellesian]]"). In these acting styles, we see a miniature version of the journey of American society during this period—and, specifically, American maleness."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/the-astonishing-power-of-the-master|title=The Astonishing Power of "The Master"|magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=September 10, 2012|access-date=April 17, 2020|archive-date=August 8, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808005959/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/the-astonishing-power-of-the-master|url-status=live}}</ref> Still other arguments regarding the film's main theme hold that it is about humanity, and man's struggle to cope with his animalistic nature. Glenn Kenny of ''MSN Movies'' wrote that the film is "Less about [Scientology's] specific set of beliefs than about how humans rely on belief systems in general to try and lift themselves out of an elemental rage, and to assert, yes, that man is not an animal."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/movies|title=The Master (2012) - Critics' reviews - MSN Movies|website=[[MSN]] |access-date=April 17, 2020|archive-date=September 18, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120918210728/http://movies.msn.com/movies/movie-critic-reviews/the-master.3/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Numerous reviewers commented on the [[Homoeroticism|homoerotic]] subtext of the film. ''[[Film Comment]]'' noted the bonding and repelling between the two men, "two edges of the split saber, play out in public and in private, in 'audits' and intimate exchanges over Freddie's alcoholic concoctions".<ref name="Jones" /> ''[[The Guardian]]'' saw "Quell's chaos and Dodd's charlatanism" locked "in a dance of death – erotic and homoerotic".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2012/nov/01/the-master-review|title=The Master – review|last=Bradshaw|first=Peter|date=November 1, 2012|work=The Guardian|access-date=November 19, 2017|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=December 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201081703/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2012/nov/01/the-master-review|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Salon (website)|Salon]]'' commented that the film contains a "not-too-veiled suggestion that Dodd's paternal yearnings for Freddie are complicated by other desires".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.salon.com/2012/09/14/the_master_a_forbidding_portrait_of_l_ron_hubbards_america/|title="The Master": A forbidding portrait of L. Ron Hubbard's America|date=September 14, 2012|work=Salon|access-date=November 19, 2017|language=en-US|archive-date=December 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201043257/https://www.salon.com/2012/09/14/the_master_a_forbidding_portrait_of_l_ron_hubbards_america/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Comparisons with Scientology===

Upon the release of the script, comparisons between the Cause and [[Scientology]] were quickly made.<ref name="NYMag3">{{cite web |last=Brown |first=Lane |title=So This New Paul Thomas Anderson Movie Is Definitely About Scientology, Right? |publisher=New York Media Holdings |work=NYMag.com |date=December 3, 2010 |url=https://nymag.com/daily/entertainment/2009/12/so_this_new_paul_thomas_anders.html |access-date=June 5, 2011 |archive-date=August 17, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110817212607/http://nymag.com/daily/entertainment/2009/12/so_this_new_paul_thomas_anders.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="NYMag">{{cite web |last=Brown |first=Lane |title=Universal Passes on Paul Thomas Anderson's Scientology Movie |publisher=New York Media Holdings |work=NYMag.com |date=March 17, 2010 |url=https://nymag.com/daily/entertainment/2010/03/why_does_paul_thomas_andersons.html |access-date=June 5, 2011 |archive-date=March 22, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100322210517/http://nymag.com/daily/entertainment/2010/03/why_does_paul_thomas_andersons.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Guardian4">{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/apr/26/scientology-hollywood-film-studio |title=Church of Scientology snaps up Hollywood film studio |last=Pilkington |first=Ed |work=[[The Guardian|Guardian.co.uk]] |publisher=[[Guardian Media Group|Guardian News and Media Limited]] |date=April 26, 2011 |access-date=June 12, 2011 |archive-date=May 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190512100455/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/apr/26/scientology-hollywood-film-studio |url-status=live }}</ref> The press noted Hoffman's physical resemblance to Scientology founder [[L. Ron Hubbard]] (1911–1986), who served in the U.S. Navy in World War II, and, after his release from the hospital, founded the belief system in 1950, the same year as the religion in the script. The film ends in England, at roughly the same time [[Saint Hill Manor]] became Hubbard's residence and the first Scientology "org".<ref name="Filming" /><ref name="NYMag3" /><ref name="Scientology"/> Also, the film's references to the need of an "able-bodied seaman" and the reference to Fred being aberrant are both terms used by Scientologists in the administrative dictionary.<ref name="screendaily">{{cite web |first=Andreas |last=Wiseman |url=http://www.screendaily.com/news/paul-thomas-anderson-on-making-the-master-scientology-was-the-least-of-our-problems/5046000.article?blocktitle=Latest-news&contentID=1846 |title=Paul Thomas Anderson on making The Master: 'Scientology was the least of our problems' |publisher=[[Screen International]] |work=ScreenDaily.com |date=September 3, 2012 |access-date=October 3, 2012 |archive-date=May 15, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190515100332/https://www.screendaily.com/news/paul-thomas-anderson-on-making-the-master-scientology-was-the-least-of-our-problems/5046000.article?blocktitle=Latest-news&contentID=1846 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The production company officially denied that the film was loosely based on Hubbard, with producer JoAnne Sellar also denying any connection to Hubbard, stating: "It's a World War II drama. It's about a drifter after World War II."<ref name="Filming" /> Harvey Weinstein also denied that the film was about Scientology: "Paul says to me the movie is about a journey for soldiers after World War II ... one of the things that happens to this soldier is he goes to a cult."<ref name="huffington">{{cite web |last=Hogan |first=Michael |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/07/26/harvey-weinstein-obama-romney-guns_n_1706394.html |title=Harvey Weinstein On Obama, Gun Control, 'The Master' And The Record-Breaking 'The Intouchables' |work=[[The Huffington Post]] |publisher=[[AOL]] |date=July 26, 2012 |access-date=July 29, 2012 |archive-date=July 28, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120728235141/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/07/26/harvey-weinstein-obama-romney-guns_n_1706394.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Anderson has stated that he has "always thought Hubbard was a great character, so interesting and larger than life, and kind of impossible to ignore",<ref name="VillageVoice">{{cite news |last=Foundas |first=Scott |title=Paul Thomas Anderson, The Master's Master |publisher=[[Village Voice Media]] |work=[[The Village Voice|VillageVoice.com]] |date=September 5, 2012 |url=http://www.villagevoice.com/content/printVersion/3698658/ |access-date=September 12, 2012 |archive-date=November 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110053739/http://www.villagevoice.com/content/printVersion/3698658/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and he acknowledges that Lancaster Dodd was inspired by Hubbard, and that he should have known that is what people would latch onto, stating: "I didn't want it to be a biography. It's not the L. Ron Hubbard story."<ref name=dailybeast/>

Several websites suggested that "important Hollywood Scientologists" objected to the project because they feared it might reveal too much about the faith, and others even speculated that the [[Church of Scientology]] had enough power to stop Universal from green-lighting the film.<ref name="Filming" /><ref name="Scientology" /> However, none of the production crew had been contacted by representatives of Scientology.<ref name="NYTimes" /> When [[Karin Pouw]], a spokeswoman for the Church of Scientology, was asked if the church had any concerns about the film, she stated, "We have not seen the film, so can't say one way or another" and that the church knew about the film only from what it read in the press.<ref name="NYTimes" /> According to Anderson, at no point did the church make any direct or indirect inquiries about the project or otherwise try to inhibit its progress,<ref name="VillageVoice"/> and that while they were making the film, Scientology was the least of their problems.<ref name="screendaily"/>

In May 2012, Anderson screened the film for his friend, actor [[Tom Cruise]], an outspoken [[Scientologist]], who had some issues with parts of the film.<ref name="Cruise">{{cite web |last=Waxman |first=Sharon |url=https://www.thewrap.com/movies/column-post/master-paul-thomas-anderson-reaches-out-scientologist-tom-cruise-exclusive-41111 |title='The Master': Paul Thomas Anderson Reaches Out to Scientologist Tom Cruise (Exclusive) |publisher=The Wrap News Inc. |work=The Wrap |date=May 22, 2012 |access-date=July 10, 2012 |archive-date=July 17, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120717082619/http://www.thewrap.com/movies/column-post/master-paul-thomas-anderson-reaches-out-scientologist-tom-cruise-exclusive-41111 |url-status=live }}</ref> Cruise had previously starred in Anderson's third film ''[[Magnolia (film)|Magnolia]]''.<ref name="72ndAA">{{cite web |url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/legacy/ceremony/72nd-winners.html |title=72nd Academy Awards Winners {{!}} Oscar Legacy |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=July 11, 2012 |archive-date=December 24, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224032622/http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/legacy/ceremony/72nd-winners.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Officials of the Church of Scientology, who reportedly heard from Cruise, "hit the roof" when they learned of a scene which suggested that the belief system was a product of the leader's imagination.<ref name="Church">{{cite web |title=Tom Cruise, other Scientology members dislike portrayal of a cult leader in new film 'The Master' |publisher=[[Daily News (New York)|New York Daily News]] |work=NYDailyNews.com |date=July 8, 2012 |access-date=July 10, 2012 |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2012/07/08/tom-cruise-other-scientology-members-dislike-portrayal-of-a-cult-leader-in-new-film-the-master/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260222162809/https://www.nydailynews.com/2012/07/08/tom-cruise-other-scientology-members-dislike-portrayal-of-a-cult-leader-in-new-film-the-master/ |archive-date=February 22, 2026}}</ref> The scene with which Cruise had issues involves Dodd's son telling Quell that Dodd is just making it up as he goes along.<ref name="Church" /> They took issue not only with this statement, but with the way it supposedly paralleled [[Ronald DeWolf|L. Ron Hubbard Jr.]]'s conflict with his own father. While church members objected to other scenes, Anderson did not excise any of them from the film.<ref name="Church" /> He stated that Cruise "did see the film. It's something between us. Everything is fine, though."
